guide.citiesinlife.start.p1:
Everything in this mod starts with the Planner Wand. You draw a box round a building you have made, choose what kind of building it is, and the mod takes it from there.

Right click one corner, right click the opposite corner, then LEFT click to confirm. Up and Down arrow change the building type before you confirm. Sneak + right click clears a selection you have changed your mind about.
guide.citiesinlife.start.p2:
Your first box must be a CITY CORE. That founds the city and asks you to name it. Everything else you register afterwards belongs to it.

Then register somewhere to live. A RESIDENTIAL box needs beds in it - one bed is one home, and a residential building with no beds houses nobody. Register a COMMERCIAL or BUSINESS box for people to work in.
guide.citiesinlife.start.p3:
The mod works out what a building holds by measuring the ENCLOSED SPACE inside your box. It needs walls, something to stand on and something overhead - a roof is what tells it the difference between a house and a field.

If it says it found no enclosed space, the box is either open to the sky or bigger than what you actually built. Draw it tighter.
guide.citiesinlife.money.p1:
Your city taxes its residents and its filled jobs every ten seconds, and pays upkeep on every chunk of land it has claimed. Claiming land you are not using is a running cost, not a free one.

Population is a number, not a crowd. The citizens you can see are a sample of it - how many walk around is a setting, and turning it down does not make your city smaller.
guide.citiesinlife.money.p2:
A city grows towards what it can support and stops when something is missing. No power, no water, or knee deep in its own rubbish all slow it down. Parks make people want to live there and raise the ceiling.

Building in creative? Press Shift+I to give your city an unlimited treasury while you plan, and again to put it back on its own money.
guide.citiesinlife.power.p1:
Power is a network you draw by hand with the Power Line Tool. Right click one machine, right click another, and a line runs between them. Sneak + right click clears a line you started by mistake.

Nothing feeds your city until it is CONNECTED. A generator standing next to your town hall with no line drawn to it produces nothing for you at all.
guide.citiesinlife.power.p2:
The generators, cheapest first: SOLAR PANELS, WINDMILLS, and a COAL PLANT - a boiler, a turbine and a chimney inside a box you register as a Turbine Power Plant. The boiler burns coal and needs water piped to it; the turbine makes the power; the chimney keeps the turbine from fouling up.

A turbine with no chimney slowly clogs, then catches fire, then explodes. The Repair Tool clears the soot.
guide.citiesinlife.power.p3:
POWER MASTS and GRID PYLONS carry a line further than machines can reach on their own. A mast is wood and cheap; a pylon is steel and reaches 250 blocks, which is what you want between one district and the next.

The long reach only counts when a mast is talking to another mast. That is what makes them the thing you build a transmission run out of.
guide.citiesinlife.water.p1:
Water has two halves. The PUMPING STATION is invisible plumbing you draw with the Pipe Line Tool: a Starter Pump standing in real water, any number of Pumps to carry it further, and an End Pump where it comes out.

The DISTRIBUTION is real pipe blocks you place. Pipes join each other on their own when they touch - the tool has no business between two pipes.
guide.citiesinlife.water.p2:
Water collects in WATER STORAGE tanks, and your city drinks from every tank standing on its own ground. An END PIPE is a tap: it pours water you can see and fill a bucket from.

VALVES let you shut a branch off. The Upgrade Tool makes a Starter Pump, an End Pump or a turbine better at its job.
guide.citiesinlife.water.p3:
Water is charged against what your buildings HOLD, not against who has moved in. A tower with room for a thousand people asks for a tower's worth of water on the day you register it.

If the city panel says you are short, you need either more pumps or fewer buildings - not more tanks. Tanks store; pumps supply.
guide.citiesinlife.sewage.p1:
Every city makes sewage simply by existing. It is the one utility that runs backwards: not a supply to keep up, but a demand to keep down. Ignore it and the rubbish piles up until nobody wants to live there.

A SEWAGE COLLECTOR takes it away. Pipe it like anything else, and give it somewhere to go - an End Pipe will pour it out, and it comes out brown.
guide.citiesinlife.sewage.p2:
WARNING. There is no such thing as a sewage pipe in this mod. A pipe is a pipe, so nothing stops you plumbing a collector onto the same run as your water tanks.

Do that and your city drinks its own sewage. People die - the population falls every ten seconds and the citizens you can see are poisoned - until you separate the two runs.
guide.citiesinlife.roads.p1:
The ROAD TOOL paints roads over blocks you have already laid. Right click two corners, left click to confirm, and press the tool's button to choose what you are painting: an ordinary street, a junction, a parking bay, a highway, or the eraser.

Streets have directions. A one-way street with no way out is a street nobody drives down.

Roads and pavement are markings rather than blocks, but they are not immune to a blast. Blow up the ground under one and the marking goes with it.
guide.citiesinlife.roads.p2:
Citizens with a long commute drive. For that they need a PARKING BAY near home and a road that actually reaches where they are going. No bay, no car - they walk instead.

HIGHWAYS are the only roads that may cross another player's land. That is what makes them highways.
guide.citiesinlife.roads.p3:
The PATH TOOL marks pavement, which is where citizens prefer to walk when they are not going anywhere in particular.

AIRPORTS are the Tourist Airplane and the Transport Airplane. Tourists arrive at one and spend money in your shops. With an International Travel pact, your citizens use them to reach another player's city.
guide.citiesinlife.services.p1:
Register a POLICE STATION, FIRE STATION, HOSPITAL, PARK, MILITARY BASE or TRANSIT STATION and it does something real, not just count towards a number.

Police catch criminals, the fire brigade puts out fires, the hospital heals, parks raise how many people want to live in your city at all.
guide.citiesinlife.services.p2:
A service needs staff. The SERVICE NPC SPAWNER inside a service building is what puts officers and doctors on the street.

A FACTORY needs workers before it produces anything, and a FACTORY OUTPUT block is where what it makes comes out. An empty factory is an expensive shed.
guide.citiesinlife.war.p1:
Declaring war costs money and tells the entire server. You will be asked to confirm, and your allies will be asked whether they are joining you.

At war, their blocks are yours to break and their people are yours to kill - and yours are theirs. Either side can make peace, and peace ends it for both at once.
guide.citiesinlife.war.p2:
The MILITARY TOOL and a MILITARY BASE let you train soldiers, which takes two minutes - so it is a decision you make before a war rather than during one.

The WAR PLANNER WAND seizes a building you have captured. It cannot turn a captured shed into a nuclear plant; you have to build one of those yourself.
guide.citiesinlife.neighbours.p1:
The Neighbours tab on the City panel is everybody else. One city at a time, with everything you can do about them.

GRANTING is one way and takes effect the moment you give it: it lets them build on your land, and does not let you build on theirs. Revoke it whenever you like.
guide.citiesinlife.neighbours.p2:
PACTS take two. The button says Propose until they have asked as well, then Accept, then End - and either side clicking End stops it that instant. There are three.

INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL lets your citizens take jobs in their city. They will only go by car on a highway or by aeroplane; they never walk across a border.
guide.citiesinlife.neighbours.p3:
HELP UTILITIES sends your surplus power and water across the border for a price you set. You only ever sell what you were not using, so a nuclear plant pays for itself. The buyer pays every step and stops receiving if they cannot.

An ALLIANCE means being asked when they go to war. Saying no costs nothing.

Your CITY FLAG is on the City panel, and the City Flag block flies it.
guide.citiesinlife.nuclear.p1:
Far more power than anything else, and the only building in the mod that can take the neighbourhood with it. Build it away from your city.

Find URANIUM ORE deep underground - rare, but in big veins when you find one. Smelt it into uranium. Draw a box round where the plant will go and register it as a NUCLEAR PLANT before you build: every reactor block reports through that registration.
guide.citiesinlife.nuclear.p2:
THE CORE. Four FUEL ROD columns per nuclear turbine, and four CONTROL ROD columns for the whole reactor. Every column the same height, at least 8 blocks, every rod block waterlogged, and a SEALING BLOCK on top of each column.

Punch any reactor block at any time and it will tell you exactly what is still wrong, with coordinates.
guide.citiesinlife.nuclear.p3:
THE COOLING LOOP, in order: pipes into the INPUT WATER port, out of the OUTPUT COOLED port, through pipes back to the INPUT COOLED port beside the uranium store, through the core, out of the OUTPUT HEATED port, and back round to the input.

The water input and the cooled output are joined by one hand-drawn link with the Pipe Line Tool. A PRESSURISED PIPE must be the last pipe on the cooled run.
guide.citiesinlife.nuclear.p4:
THE CONTROLS. TURBINE POWER is the master dial - at zero the plant makes nothing and cannot explode, and that is a guarantee. COOLER adds cooling. HEAT pulls the rods out for more power and much more risk. PRESSURE is the relief valve: it drops the pressure fast and costs you output while it is open.

The MAIN MONITOR shows temperature, pressure and what is wrong. An ALARM inside the box goes amber and then red.
guide.citiesinlife.nuclear.p5:
A URANIUM STORAGE block feeds the rods automatically - right click it with uranium. A STEAM EMITTER is the chimney: without one the cooling ports foul up and clog. When the core is over its limits the rods get loud and the sealing blocks vent steam through the roof, which you can see from outside the building.

If it melts down, RUN. The pipes go, then the turbines, then the core, then a crater about eighty blocks across. The fallout reaches five hundred blocks, lasts ten minutes and harms EVERYTHING alive in it - your own citizens included. Only creative mode is exempt.

The crater takes the roads, the pavement and the Planner Wand boxes with it. A building that is no longer a building loses its registration.
screen.citiesinlife.peace_offer_body: %s has offered you a peace treaty. Accepting ends the war for both of you. Refusing carries it on, and they will be told. You can decide later from the Neighbours tab.

message.citiesinlife.peace_offered_to_yo: %s has offered you a peace treaty.
message.citiesinlife.peace_declined: You refused %s's treaty. The war continues.
message.citiesinlife.peace_declined_by: %s refused your treaty. The war continues.

guide.citiesinlife.services.p3:
The three emergency services DRIVE. A staffed police station, fire station or hospital keeps somebody on whether or not anything is happening, and when a call comes in from further away than a citizen would walk, they take a vehicle to it.

A POLICE CAR, a FIRE TRUCK and an AMBULANCE, each with its own light bar and siren. They need a road within about thirty blocks of the station - no road outside, no vehicle - and they use the same setting that switches citizens' cars on and off.

Nobody vanishes on the spot any more. A worker who has run out of things to do walks back to the station and goes in at the door, and so does a tourist whose visit is over.
guide.citiesinlife.war.p3:
War runs in PHASES. Whoever declared attacks first, and the sides swap every three minutes, so you are never attacking and defending at the same time.

Attackers march on the enemy and plant charges. DEFENDERS DIG IN - they cut a trench and hold it, and they never plant charges of their own. Both sides work this out from who declared and when, so both agree about whose turn it is.

Peace is an OFFER, not a switch. Send a peace treaty and the other side gets to accept or refuse it. The offer waits for them even if they are offline.
guide.citiesinlife.settings.p1:
The mod has its own SETTINGS screen, reached from the button at the top right of the City panel. It is there because the ordinary config cannot be opened while you are connected to a server - and hosting your own world through Essential counts as connected.

Only the owner of the world can change what the world does: how many citizens walk around, whether cars are on and how far they drive, how big a meltdown is, how tall the steam plume goes, and whether operators ignore city borders. Everybody else can look.

CITIZENS and CARS are the two that cost frames. STEAM PLUME is the first thing to turn down on a machine that is struggling.
guide.citiesinlife.settings.p2:
The bottom row, MACHINE VOLUME, is yours alone. It saves the moment you click it and works even when the rest of the screen is greyed out, because how loud a turbine is in your ears is not a fact about the world. Set it to 0 to switch the lot off.

What makes a noise: turbines, and the nuclear one follows its power dial in both loudness and pitch. Coal boilers, starter pumps that are actually touching water, windmills, and a faint buzz off masts and pylons.

Rods buzz quietly and get very loud at critical. Desks and tills only sound when somebody is genuinely working there. Houses, shops and offices murmur when they have people in them - and go quiet when they do not.
